questions.q: What is the main reason to wrap an API in a client class instead of calling requests.post everywhere it's needed?
options: Classes run faster than functions in Python
It centralizes shared setup (auth, base URL, retries) in one place instead of twenty
requests.post cannot be used outside a class
It's required by the Messages API
questions.explain: A client class means a change to auth, headers, or retry logic happens in one place, not scattered across every call site.

questions.q: What typically gets set up in a client class's __init__ method?
options: The specific prompt text for one particular call
Shared config used on every call: API key, base URL, and a reusable session
The final parsed response from the API
Nothing — __init__ should always be empty
questions.explain: __init__ is where one-time, shared setup happens: credentials, base URL, and a Session that gets reused across every method call.

questions.q: What advantage does requests.Session() have over calling requests.post() directly each time?
options: It reuses the underlying connection and headers across multiple calls
It automatically retries failed requests forever
It removes the need for an API key
It converts JSON responses into XML
questions.explain: A Session reuses the connection (and configured headers) rather than rebuilding everything from scratch on every single call.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where should one-off logic like 'what prompt to send this time' live?
options: Hardcoded inside __init__
Inside the client class's send_message method
In the calling code, not inside the client class itself
It must be stored in an environment variable
questions.explain: Shared, reused-everywhere logic belongs on the class; one-off decisions specific to a single script stay in the calling code.

questions.q: What does resp.raise_for_status() do in the send_message method?
options: It prints the response body to the console
It raises an exception if the response's HTTP status is 4xx or 5xx
It retries the request automatically
It converts the response into a client instance
questions.explain: raise_for_status() is a requests library method that raises an HTTPError for 4xx/5xx responses, surfacing failures instead of silently returning bad data.
